The shim owns the container's stdio and reaps its exit code, and it stays alive across a daemon restart. This is what makes `systemctl restart docker` survivable on a production host, and it is why `live-restore` exists as a daemon option to make it explicit.

One API call runs `-v /:/host --privileged`, and now you have the host. This is why adding a user to the `docker` group is granting root, why mounting the socket into a container is a serious decision, and why rootless mode exists.
